thread:
maya: quick heads-up — brought up open-embed-3b quantized to int8 on the ecommerce eval suite (10k pairs). seeing a consistent recall@5 drop vs redwood-embed-1.

sam: how big is the drop? numbers?

maya: R@1: 0.71 -> 0.68, R@5: 0.92 -> 0.89. average cosine similarity down ~0.02. small but consistent across categories.

eli: did you apply L2-normalization post-quant? int8 can change norms and that messes up cosine.

maya: yes, pipeline does `normalize=True` after dequant. I also retried forcing fp16 and the numbers went back to baseline.

ciara: can you paste the eval command and index settings? might be faiss params.

maya: sure — run we used:
```
./run_eval --model open-embed-3b --quant int8 --dataset ecommerce-10k \
  --metric recall@k --k 5 --index hnsw --normalize
```

maya: index was HNSW with ef_search=128, M=32. same index used for the fp16 run.

sam: two hypotheses — 1) quantization noise for long-tail tokens changes embedding space topology; 2) internal fallback to dot-product scoring somewhere (if norm drift occurs). can you dump pairwise norms distribution?

ciara: I have a quick dump. sample norms (fp16 -> int8):
```
fp16 mean_norm=1.002, std=0.048
int8 mean_norm=0.987, std=0.081
```
so int8 has larger variance — could explain small cosine shifts.

eli: try doing a small post-quant calibration: compute a scaling factor per-dim using a heldout set (a linear rescale) or re-normalize per-batch and see effect.

maya: did that: global per-dim rescale improved R@5 by +0.01 but didn't fully recover.

eval-bot: automated-eval: open-embed-3b int8 on ecommerce-10k — R@1:0.68 R@5:0.89 MAP:0.74 latency p50:6.2ms p95:26ms

ciara: latency looks great though. if we need production cost wins, int8 is attractive. but we need to hit parity.

sam: also check nearest-neighbor tie handling and distance thresholds in retrieval code. HNSW uses approximate distances; slight shifts can change boundary cases.

maya: good point. re-ran with exact IVF flat search (brute within buckets): results closer to fp16 but still -0.005 on R@5.

eli: what's the dataset breakdown? maybe certain categories (e.g., fashion titles with many short tokens) degrade more.

ciara: breakdown: fashion R@5 drop 0.04, electronics 0.01, home 0.005. fashion looks bad.

maya: fashion titles are short & heavy on brand tokens — maybe tokenization differences amplify quant noise.

sam: try vocabulary-aware quant: do per-embedding-block quantization (grouped quant) rather than flat int8. sometimes reduces distortion on sparse-dominated dims.

maya: scheduling an experiment for grouped-quant and also a run with whitening PCA fitted on fp16 then applied to int8 outputs.

ciara: for reproducibility, command snippets:
```
# baseline fp16
./run_eval --model open-embed-3b --precision fp16 --dataset ecommerce-10k --index hnsw

# int8 grouped-quant
./run_eval --model open-embed-3b --quant int8 --quant-scheme grouped --group-size 64 \
  --dataset ecommerce-10k --index hnsw
```

maya: will push logs to the /eval-results bucket and post link when done. tagging @ciara @eli for follow-ups. if grouped-quant recovers >0.02 R@5 we can consider int8 rollout with caveats.

sam: also add a small synthetic parity test: identical pairs (should be near-1.0 cosine). if those break, it's a hard fail.

maya: good call — added that. quick local check: identical-pair cosine mean: fp16 0.998, int8 0.994. not catastrophic but noticeable.

eli: ok next steps: (1) grouped quant experiment, (2) whitening/PCA calibration, (3) exact-NN re-check, (4) per-category diagnostics. if any fix recovers >=0.015 R@5 we can A/B.

ciara: I'll surface these in the model-onboarding doc and add a QA checklist: tokenization parity, norm distribution, parity test, per-cat breakdown, faiss-config snapshot.

maya: thanks. i'll post raw plots (norm hist, recall curves) in the thread once uploaded. :thumbsup:

ciara: also leaving a note — watch for false positives in de-dup pipeline if similarity thresholds assumed from fp16. may need to shift thresholds slightly for int8.

maya: noted. closing loop here once grouped-quant runs finish.
